title: Standardization of Input-Output Coefficient Declaration
summary: The concept of 'quantities of materials' evolved from a basic declaration format for specific industries into a formalized regulatory requirement known as 'Upokoron-Utpad Sohog' (Input-Output Coefficient). Over time, the procedure became standardized across various sectors (electronics, appliances, construction) and eventually integrated into the broader legal framework of the Customs Act, 2023.

evolution.legal_basis: Shifted from industry-specific administrative directives to a codified requirement under the Customs Act, 2023.
evolution.procedure: Transitioned from simple declaration forms to a rigorous multi-copy approval process involving the Commissioner and NBR.
evolution.scope: Expanded from specific consumer electronics to include industrial construction materials and general warehousing operations.

timeline.change: Initial introduction of a standardized declaration table for cellular phone production.
Formalized the 'Input-Output Coefficient' (Upokoron-Utpad Sohog) submission process, requiring Commissioner approval and submission of 3 copies for customs clearance.
Extension of the standardized coefficient declaration model to the pre-fabricated building industry.
Refinement of the administrative reporting line, directing copies to the NBR Member (Customs: Policy and ICT).
Codification of 'Import Availability' and 'Utilization Permission' (UP) within the Customs Act, 2023, providing a legal basis for material quantity calculations.

National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue is the regulatory authority requiring the submission of a formal declaration for goods, parts, or materials used in the manufacture or assembly of cellular phones.
Cellular Phone Manufacturing and Assembl: Manufacturers are required to provide a detailed declaration regarding the raw materials, parts, and components used in the production process, including their respective Harmonized System (HS) codes.

The declaration must specify usage quantities per unit of production, accounting for both net requirements and wastage percentages, and requires verification via countersignature by the relevant Value Added Tax Commissioner.
Value Added Tax Registration: Entities engaged in the manufacturing or assembly of cellular phones must provide their official Value Added Tax registration number as part of the formal declaration process.

member_objects.resolved_text: ৩। লিফট উৎপাদনকারী কর্তৃক প্রতি একক লিফট উৎপাদনের জন্য সম্ভাব্য বা যৌক্তিক অপচয়সহ কি কি উপকরণ কি পরিমাণে আবশ্যক (উপকরণ-উৎপাদ সহগ) সে সম্পর্কিত তথ্য “পরিশিষ্ট-২” অনুযায়ী ৩ (তিন) কপি পণ্য আমদানির পূর্বেই সংশ্লিষ্ট ভ্যাট কমিশনারেট এর কমিশনার বরাবর দাখিল করিতে হইবে। কমিশনার উক্ত উপকরণ-উৎপাদ সহগ অনুমোদনপূর্বক প্রতিস্বাক্ষর করিবেন এবং একটি কপি অফিসের রেকর্ড হিসাবে সংরক্ষণ করিবেন, দ্বিতীয় কপি জাতীয় রাজস্ব বোর্ডের সদস্য (কাস্টমস নীতি) বরাবরে প্রেরণ করিবেন এবং অপর কপি প্রতিষ্ঠান কর্তৃপক্ষকে ফেরত দিবেন। “পরিশিষ্ট-২” এর সত্যায়িত ফটোকপি প্রতিটি পণ্যচালান খালাসের সময় বিল অফ এন্ট্রির সহিত দাখিল করিতে হইবে।

Input-Output Coefficient: Manufacturers of lifts are required to submit three copies of the input-output coefficient to the Commissioner of the concerned VAT Commissionerate prior to the importation of goods.
The coefficient statement must detail the required quantities of materials and permitted waste per unit of lift production in accordance with the specified appendix.
The certified photocopy of this document must be submitted along with the bill of entry during the clearance of each consignment of goods.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner is responsible for reviewing, approving, and countersigning the input-output coefficient documents submitted by lift manufacturers.
National Board of Revenue: The Commissioner must forward one copy of the approved input-output coefficient to the Member (Customs Policy) of the National Board of Revenue.
Bill of Entry: A certified copy of the approved input-output coefficient must be attached to the bill of entry for each imported consignment at the time of customs clearance.

member_objects.resolved_text: ৫। প্রতি একক পণ্য উৎপাদনের জন্য সম্ভাব্য বা যৌক্তিক অপচয়সহ কি কি পণ্য বা উপকরণ কি পরিমাণে আবশ্যক (উপকরণ-উৎপাদ সহগ) সে সম্পর্কিত তথ্য “পরিশিষ্ট-২” অনুযায়ী ৩ (তিন) কপি পণ্য আমদানির পূর্বেই সংশ্লিষ্ট ভ্যাট কমিশনারেট এর কমিশনার বরাবর দাখিল করিতে হইবে। কমিশনার উক্ত সহগ অনুমোদনপূর্বক প্রতিস্বাক্ষর করিবেন এবং একটি কপি অফিসের রেকর্ড হিসাবে সংরক্ষণ করিবেন, দ্বিতীয় কপি জাতীয় রাজস্ব বোর্ডের সদস্য (কাস্টমস নীতি) বরাবরে প্রেরণ করিবেন এবং অপর কপি প্রতিষ্ঠান কর্তৃপক্ষকে ফেরত দিবেন। পরিশিষ্ট-২ এর সত্যায়িত ফটোকপি প্রতিটি আমদানি পণ্যচালান খালাসের সময় বিল অব এন্ট্রির সহিত দাখিল করিতে হইবে।

Input-Output Coefficient: Manufacturers are required to submit information regarding the quantity and potential waste of materials needed for unit production, known as the input-output coefficient, to the Commissioner of the relevant VAT Commissionerate.
The submission must be made in triplicate prior to the importation of raw materials as per the specified format.
A certified copy of this document must be attached to the bill of entry for every consignment at the time of customs clearance.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner is responsible for reviewing and approving the input-output coefficient submitted by an industrial establishment.

Upon approval, the Commissioner must sign the documents, retain one copy for office records, forward a copy to the Member (Customs Policy) of the National Board of Revenue, and return the final copy to the applicant.
National Board of Revenue: The Member (Customs Policy) of the National Board of Revenue receives a copy of the approved input-output coefficient documentation from the Commissioner of the relevant VAT Commissionerate for administrative and monitoring purposes.
Bill of Entry: The importer is mandated to attach a certified photocopy of the approved input-output coefficient documentation to the bill of entry during the clearance process for each import consignment.

National Board of Revenue: Commissioner of the relevant VAT Commissionerate

Input-Output Coefficient: Pre-fabricated building manufacturers must submit information regarding the quantity and types of materials required for production, including reasonable waste, as specified in the relevant appendix.
The submission must be made in triplicate to the Commissioner of the concerned VAT Commissionerate prior to the importation of goods.
Commissioner of VAT Commissionerate: The Commissioner is responsible for reviewing and approving the Input-Output Coefficient and must countersign the submitted documents.
The Commissioner must distribute the approved copies to the National Board of Revenue and the importing institution, while retaining one for office records.
National Board of Revenue: The Member (Customs Policy) of the National Board of Revenue receives a copy of the approved Input-Output Coefficient from the VAT Commissionerate.
Bill of Entry: A certified copy of the approved Input-Output Coefficient must be attached to the Bill of Entry at the time of customs clearance for each consignment of imported goods.

Input-Output Coefficient: Refrigerator and freezer manufacturers or vendors must declare the specific quantities and types of materials required for production, including reasonable wastage, in the format prescribed in the appendix.
The approved Input-Output Coefficient must be submitted in three copies to the relevant Commissioner of Customs before the import of goods for customs clearance purposes.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner is responsible for reviewing, approving, and countersigning the submitted Input-Output Coefficient for refrigerator and freezer production.
Upon approval, the Commissioner must retain one copy for office records, forward a second copy to the National Board of Revenue, and return the third copy to the manufacturing entity.
National Board of Revenue: A copy of the approved Input-Output Coefficient must be formally transmitted by the Commissioner of Customs to the member of the National Board of Revenue responsible for Customs Policy and ICT.
Bill of Entry: Importers are required to attach an authenticated photocopy of the approved Input-Output Coefficient to the Bill of Entry at the time of customs clearance for each consignment of materials.

Customs Act 2023: The term Act is defined as the Customs Act 2023 for the purposes of these rules.
Import Eligibility: Import eligibility is defined as the quantity of raw materials that may be imported under warehousing facilities, determined based on the approved annual production capacity of machinery and the projected consumption of raw materials.
Utilization Permission: Utilization Permission is defined as the authorization issued by the customs authorities to produce goods using duty-free raw materials imported under the warehousing system and properly bonded, in accordance with the provisions of the Customs Act.
Raw Materials: Raw materials are defined as those imported or locally procured in accordance with existing regulations for the purpose of producing goods for export.
Schedule: The term Schedule is defined as any schedule contained within these rules.
Directorate: The term Directorate is defined as the Directorate of Customs Duty Exemption and Drawback.
Input-Output Coefficient: The term Coefficient refers to a declaration approved by the appropriate authority detailing the description and quantity of raw materials required to produce a single unit of finished goods.

Directorate: Directorate of Customs Duty Exemption and Drawback
